To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we are able to predict corporate earnings from publicly available data with a correlation to human analysts' predictions that is higher than the one between the analysts' predictions themselves and 2) we are able, with our model, to beat human analysts in predicting the earnings of S&P 100 firms in 2012.

a) a simple linear regression on publicly available stock market data can predict corporate earnings with a mean absolute error of 2.8% and a median absolute error of 1.8%; b) the approach is able to outperform human analysts by 2% on average; c) the approach is robust with respect to different time horizons and different companies.

a) the prediction of corporate earnings is feasible with machine learning, that b) the earnings of S&P 100 firms can be forecasted with a median accuracy of 4.4%, which c) outperforms human analysts in the test period from 2010 to 2012 by an average of 0.6% and d) can even be further improved by the addition of a human in the loop.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new application of machine learning methods to the prediction of corporate earnings and with the question whether now casting is a viable alternative to traditional methods in this domain.

a) the development of an automatic nowcasting method, b) the identification of the most important features for earnings prediction, and c) the evaluation of the method against the performance of human analysts.
the question whether it is possible to create accurate earnings forecasts based on publicly observable data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented method is a first step towards a fully automatized earnings prediction system that is based on publicly available data only.
our approach is a step towards the automation of the earnings prediction task, which is a first step towards a fully automatized investment management.
our method outperforms analysts in the sense that we are better in predicting the direction of the change in corporate earnings, i.e., whether earnings will go up, down or stay the same.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stock market contains valuable information about corporate earnings that is currently neglected.
the prediction of corporate earnings is a solvable problem that can be solved by using publicly observable data.
we show that it is possible to predict corporate earnings from public stock price and correlation data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the fact that the earnings prediction problem is very complex and has been considered intractable by the research community, it is possible to create a simple yet accurate model for predicting corporate earnings.
now casting can be applied not only to macroeconomic variables such as GDP or unemployment rates, but also to microeconomic data such as corporate earnings.
the stock market contains valuable information for earnings predictions that is not used by current machine learning approaches.
